deities: Shiva (Sivalinga within a circular yonipitha); subsidiary shrines of Ganesha, Parvati, Kartikeya

history.summary: Budharaja Temple is a Shiva temple atop Budharaja hillock in the middle of Sambalpur city. The IGNCA/ASI survey dates it to the first quarter of the 18th century under Chauhan rule; a temple history account says it was initiated by King Chhatrasal (1690-1705, 7th Chauhan ruler of Sambalpur) and completed by his son King Ajit Singh, built to commemorate the death of prince Burha Rai (hence 'Burharai'). CONFLICT (verify): one travel blog claims 14th-15th century construction under Balaram Dev, which disagrees with both IGNCA and the Chhatrasal/Ajit Singh account. Architecture: rekha vimana, pidha jagamohana, open pillared mandapa; twelve-armed dancing Shiva and eight-armed Mahisasuramardini reliefs in the jagamohana. The hill is tied to the 1857 revolt of Veer Surendra Sai, who used it to watch British troop movements; a well with an alleged secret tunnel to the old royal quarters (Raja Bakhri, Rani Bakhri) and a Shahid Stambha (martyrs' memorial) stand by the temple. NOTE: id 'budharaja-temple' is already used by a DIFFERENT Budharaja shrine in Papanga, Bargarh (seq 1965), so this file uses 'budharaja-temple-sambalpur'. NO reliable image of the actual temple was found after image searching, so media is empty.

town_description: Sambalpur is the commercial and cultural capital of western Odisha, lying on the Mahanadi river about 320 km northwest of Bhubaneswar. It is famous for the Sambalpuri ikat textile tradition, the Hirakud Dam (one of the longest earthen dams in the world, ~15 km away), and its role in the freedom struggle led by Veer Surendra Sai. Sambalpur is named after Goddess Samaleswari, its presiding deity.
